title: The Effects of Stress in the Formation of Grain Boundary Oxides on Ni-5Cr Alloys in a Rhines Pack Environment
content: Nickel (Ni)-based alloys are extensively used in extreme environments, including those in light water reactors (LWRs), due to their exceptional resistance to corrosion and creep, especially at high temperatures. Chromium (Cr) is a crucial alloying element that promotes the formation of a dense protective oxide film that enhances oxidation and corrosion resistance while mitigating intergranular (IG) stress corrosion cracking (SCC). In Ni-Cr binary alloys, particularly those with low Cr concentrations, grain boundaries (GBs) play a critical role in oxidation response [1-3]. Both IG oxide penetration along GBs and protective oxide 'caps' formed on the top of GBs have been observed [4]. However, the influence of the stress state and the role of GBs in oxidation behavior remains poorly understood. Elucidating the impact of stress on oxidation at GBs is essential for developing a mechanistic understanding of SCC in these systems, which is crucial for improving the durability and reliability of Ni-Cr alloys in extreme environments where stress and chemical conditions are present.
